subject.title: Slug alias quota (25) blocking legitimate naming migration — publisher nitishgargiitd

question: After verifying that `nitishgargiitd` controls the publisher account and the 13 listed destination slugs, should ClawHub grant a one-time audited redirect exception, or require the publisher to release existing aliases under a defined retention policy?
rationale: The limit is a deliberate ownership and anti-squatting safeguard, so source inspection cannot determine the acceptable migration exception or retention tradeoff without maintainer policy intent.

options.title: Grant a scoped audited exception
options.body: Authorize exactly the 13 enumerated old-to-new aliases after account verification, preserve the global 25-alias cap, and record the operator action.

options.title: Require alias release first
options.body: Keep the cap strict and ask the publisher to identify existing redirects that can be removed under a documented traffic or retention criterion.

options.title: Define a reusable migration policy
options.body: Create a documented, approval-gated migration allowance for verified publishers before resolving this request.

recommendation.title: Grant a scoped audited exception
recommendation.body: Authorize exactly the 13 enumerated old-to-new aliases after account verification, preserve the global 25-alias cap, and record the operator action.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged slug-protection work is the strongest available provenance for the policy boundary involved.
